notes: T671 — store-write contention (operator proposal: per-row files + tasks.json as index). DESIGN-ONLY outcome, and that is the honest one: the design half is where the brief said the value is, and it concludes the full per-row migration is NOT worth its cost now. Three load-bearing findings. (1) The duplicate-T-ID silent-loss class the operator names is ALREADY CLOSED by T545 (2026-08-20): all 24 store writers now follow lock→read→modify→write→unlock, and cmdAdd re-reads under that flock and refuses 'task <id> already exists' (src/managent/main.zig:2962); add --auto bumps _sys.next_id under the same flock. The operator's scenario — 'two writers each read a store lacking T999, each write it, the loser disappears' — is the PRE-T545 shape; two concurrent registrations of one id today yield exactly one success + one loud exit-1 refusal. (2) Per-row files would make the contention SHRINK (row writes independent; the 527 KB whole-file rewrite becomes a ~50-byte _sys counter bump) but NOT vanish: _sys.directive_next (tell), _sys.assertion_next (assert), _sys.next_id (add --auto), _sys.closes (done) are still a shared monotonic counter that must serialize on some shared file. Inventory: tasks.json 527 KB/338 rows + archive.json 104 KB/115 rows (both whole-file RMW under flock), directives.jsonl 393 lines + assertion-ledger (both append-only, already outside the store). The brief's §3 'killed_by records ruling 32 depends on' are in untracked/runs/*.json, NOT tasks.json — unaffected by any store migration. (3) THE REAL SHARP EDGE (recommended fix): the silent empty-store hazard. parseStateJson returns an empty StateMap when content trims empty OR is exactly '{}' (main.zig:1944-1946) and returns empty state when content is valid JSON but not an object — null/[]/42/'x' (:1959); readState returns empty only on FileNotFound. The startup migration block then sees sys_duty_migrated==false and WRITES the empty state back as an _sys-only store on EVERY invocation (read-only verbs included) — so a store that is empty, {}, or any valid non-object JSON is silently replaced by an empty kanban, all 338 rows destroyed with no error. This is the D046 shape and the brief's 'never a silently empty store' control. Invalid JSON does fail loudly (parse errors); the silent cases are empty/{}/valid-non-object. Fix is small: readState distinguishes file-absent (legit empty) from file-present-but-content-is-not-a-valid-object-carrying-_sys (corruption → loud exit, no migration write); a managent-written store ALWAYS carries _sys (serializeState emits it even for zero rows), so 'present but no _sys' is unambiguously corruption. DESIGN DECISION on where row state lives (brief §2): option B — status moves to the per-row file, index = id→path + _sys only; rejected A (status stays in index ⇒ claim/close still write the shared file, no gain) and C (index status cache ⇒ reintroduces the stored-vs-derived drift class). Cost of B: status/show/orient/next/claim/done all read N+1 files (fine at 338; trivial sub-ms), and crash consistency is STRICTLY BETTER (write row file, fsync, then atomic-rename index; a crash leaves a harmless orphan row, vs today's total loss on a torn store). Sibling defect re-confirmed and still open: _sync/_standing are raw string surgery (writeSyncData/persistStandingState), dropped by any later writeStateLocked (parser skips _-keys, serializer never emits them) — T545 recorded it, still unfixed; sharding without first-classing these two keys moves the defect, not fixes it. PRIOR ART read (brief §5): T545 (lock class), T587 (write path already serialize→parse-back→atomic-rename, so the empty-store hazard is external and needs a READ-side guard), T650 (the same append/never-overwrite instinct, landed for run records — proof the operator's instinct is sound in general, wrong next target for the store). WHY NO CODE: src/managent/main.zig is live-held by T636 (row-shape, in progress on the same file, run records through 20:55Z) — the one-writer invariant forbids a concurrent edit — AND the design's own verdict is that the migration is not the right next step. Deliverable src/managent/main.zig is deliberately untouched (declared but not modified); the committed design doc docs/infra/managent/store-sharding-design.md is the durable artifact. RECOMMENDED FOLLOW-UP (mutation, sequenced after T636 releases main.zig): implement the silent-empty-store guard test-first (empty/{}/[]/null/truncated arms, assert loud non-zero exit and no overwrite), wire into zig build test. Per-row files remain the right END state if a 5×5-era fleet makes contention the measured bottleneck; the design doc is the spec to build against then.
